content.content: deccy new -m <summary> --on <id>... [--evaluates <id>...] opens a change after the named dependencies, writes the node file named by the new change id, and describes the change with the summary (ylvpykys, oyxxypuz, yuznnnlx). It stays one invocation of the one verb: the verb reads -m, --on and --evaluates after itself as its own arguments, and the invocation-level CLI interprets none of their values (wzmmmmsw). --on is unchanged — repeatable, and required for this birth — the new node naming the given ids in depends_on and no others (msyrpuol). --evaluates is repeatable and optional, each occurrence naming one node the new node checks; it lands within the same invocation, so a birth made with it carries in evaluates exactly the ids given there — none dropped, none added, and none of them in depends_on — each occurrence contributing that one evaluates edge to the node being born and nothing else. Nothing else about the birth moves: not the change opened or how it is bracketed, not which node file is written or how many, not placement, not -m or the summary it sets, not the content the node carries (rkqztuuw), and --evaluates never stands in for --on or makes a birth reachable without placement. An id named by --evaluates may name a decision or an evaluation, the evaluates relation admitting both targets (volxoyyy); so the flag tells no kind apart, no birth is refused or special-cased because a named id names an evaluation rather than a decision or the reverse, and the born node's kind follows the kind rule as before (pzquqmrq). Its ids are resolved as what they name — the nodes the born node checks — not by inheriting the resolution --on's ids go through, which carries a special case belonging to depends_on that --evaluates has no claim on (volxoyyy).
content.rationale: Flags mirror the creation steps so there is no second way to create — --evaluates is a surface over the evaluates edge a birth already lands, not a second creation — and requiring --on keeps every birth placed; the checks-naming ids get their own resolution rather than borrowing depends_on's special case.
